I watched it, and it was accurate-ish to the actual manga, but they added some other characters I barely remembered. I remember a scene where the two main characters, Johnny and Gyro were riding on two horses together, but it was animated in a style that was so painfully illumination. The scene that everyone was flaming online was Gyro's reveal, which the design looked spot on , but everyone said his nose was too long, and it looked stupid. I don't know why I dreamed something like SBR would be animated by Illumination. But even non-jojo fans were flaming the design like how people flamed ugly sonic, but they didn't change it?? And in the movie trailer Johnny was walking half of the time, and then in a wheelchair in the next scene. I then scrolled down to another video, which was kind of like how people memed the Minecraft movie trailer. I VIVIDLY remember this. I've just finished SBR, so I'm finally gonna ask - what was the whole point of the true man's world arc?

First of all, a mandatory "it was so peak". Now to get to the point, I've read all of SBR, but due to a pretty bizarre translation situation I had to read it in Italian, which I'm not exactly fluent in (yet), but understood almost all of the manga, with just a few exceptions. One of them is the whole true man's world arc, which was written in such language that I didn't completely get everything. So I'll just ask, what exactly was the true man's world supposed to be? I don't think I've seen anything about it a single time past the defeat of Ringo. Was it all just a lesson for gyro about fair duels? I'm wondering because I don't know if I'm just a moron and didn't understand it, or it's just *bizarre*

Is the doomposting right?

I’ll be honest: I’ve noticed people online complaining about the many cut scenes—specifically those involving Pocoloco, Sandman, and the Lucy/Steven/Mountain Tim trio. They’re saying David Pro shouldn't touch JoJolion and that the JoJo anime should be cancelled, but I honestly think they’re overreacting. Regarding Sandman, we knew the scene would be moved even before the first episode aired; people claim his character now lacks motivation or appeal, yet he remains a favorite among those who haven't read the manga. As for Pocoloco, many complain that the racist undertones in the conversation with his father were removed—claiming the anime lacks the courage to tackle such topics—and point to similar issues regarding Lucy’s age (which wasn't mentioned) and a line of Tim’s that was altered. I don't think it's fair to say David Pro is incapable of handling these themes, especially considering they adapted the racism directed at Smokey and the entire Orangutan arc. People who keep comparing it to the manga need to remember that this is an adaptation; cutting or rearranging scenes is normal, and with over 40 episodes still to go, judging it now makes no sense. That’s just my opinion, though—feel free to disagree.
